_README: The git-side half of the Correlix corresponding-source archive: what is
archived, where its bytes are, what they hash to, when that was last
proven, and until when the object is locked.
It holds NO credential and NO signed URL. An object key is not a secret
and is useless without a role; a presigned URL is a bearer token and is
never written to a file in this repository.
Read by `source-archive.py release-fetch` (which refuses to place an
artifact this file does not vouch for), `audit`, `verify` and
_state: EMPTY. No artifact has been ingested yet: the company AWS account, bucket and
roles do not exist (tracker 262, blocked on the owner). The tooling, the IaC
and the tests are complete and were proven end to end against a local
S3-compatible stand-in; the first real ingest fills this file.
Until then every release continues to take its corresponding source from the
copies retained in git and, for the nine large tarballs, from the pinned
upstream URL — which is exactly the gap this archive closes.
